title: Bellarmino’s ‘by praying only’ sense fails prayers that ask by command, precept, and power
source_text: LVIII. Verum modo allati Bellarmini expositio, qua dicit preces ad Sanctos conceptas, quibuscunque verbis exprimantur, hunc sensum habere, secundum Ecclesiae Romanae mentem, ut Sancti quae postulantur, praestent orando, atque impetrando, non alia vero ratione: haec, inquam, expositio non satis quadrat illis ad Sanctos orationibus, in quibus non simpliciter rogantur ut peccata solvant, corda sanctificent, & caelum aperiant, sed ut id faciant jussu, praecepto, potestate: quales orationes in publico cultu Ecclesiae Romanae non paucae reperiuntur.
pass_a_gloss: But the exposition of Bellarmine just now adduced, by which he says that prayers conceived to the Saints, by whatever words they are expressed, have this sense according to the mind of the Roman Church, that the Saints furnish what is asked by praying and obtaining, but not in any other way: this exposition, I say, does not sufficiently square with those prayers to the Saints in which they are not simply asked to loose sins, sanctify hearts, and open heaven, but to do that by command, precept, power: of which kind not a few prayers are found in the public cult of the Roman Church.
pass_b_english: Bellarmino’s ‘they only pray it in’ reading does not fit public texts.
Some hymns ask Saints to act by command, precept, and power—not merely by obtaining.

choices.why: Marks the stronger public-cult petitions Le Blanc flags.
